interface.title: Fisheye Canopy Analyzer (hemispheR-py Streamlit app)
interface.field: Plant ecology / agronomy, canopy structure remote sensing
interface.stage_of_work: Data processing and analysis of field hemispherical (fisheye) canopy photographs
interface.what_it_is_for: Turn one fisheye canopy photo into gap fraction, effective and true leaf area index, clumping indices and mean leaf tilt angle by setting a circular lens mask and binarization and gap-fraction settings, then running a four-step Import → Binarize → Gap Fraction → Canopy Attributes pipeline.

data.note: P072.jpg (3072×4096, portrait) was used for most of the work. P042b.jpg (4096×3072, landscape) was uploaded later as a second image and replaced the first, because the uploader holds one file at a time. On P072 the auto-detected mask (1536, 2048, r=1534) is the image centre with r ≈ half the width. It took in black area outside the lens and gave Le 0.52. A manual mask (1536, 2400, r=1420) gave Le 1.03, L 1.17, LX 0.88, DIFN 48.4%. Zonal Otsu gave Le 1.05, L 1.19, LX 0.88, DIFN 47.7%, which matches the README's expected Le≈1.04, L≈1.21, LX≈0.86, DIFN≈47.7%. The P042b run was not at default settings: it kept the equidistant lens, End VZA 60 and 6 zenith rings from earlier runs, and gave Le 1.53, L 1.58, LX 0.97, DIFN 36.3% (the README gives Le 1.32, L 1.36, LX 0.97, DIFN 38% at defaults).

features.name: Circular region-of-interest mask with live preview
features.general: Lay a circle over an image to mark the valid area. Either type its centre and radius, or nudge an auto-guessed circle in set steps. Check the overlay and the coverage figure, then pass the circle to the analysis.
features.specific: Under Mask source, choose Auto-detect (centre/half-width guess, with ←/→, ↑/↓, ⊖/⊕ tap buttons, Step size per tap and ← Reset to Auto) or Manual (xc/yc/rc number inputs). The Mask Preview expander redraws the red circle over the photo and shows image W/H, xc, yc, rc and Mask coverage %. Changing the mask clears earlier results, and Edit Mask & Re-run reopens the preview.
steps: Upload the image; the preview shows the auto circle
Choose Auto-detect or Manual mask source
Type xc/yc/rc, or set a step size and tap the nudge buttons
Check the red circle and Mask coverage % in the preview
Press Run Analysis; the Import Log confirms the mask is valid
serves_tasks: Outline the part of the image that holds real data, and check it rather than trusting the automatic guess
Analyse a second photo, redoing the outline because its automatic one is off-centre

features.name: Threshold-method selector with binary image and gap/canopy split
features.general: Split an image into two classes with an automatic global threshold, an automatic threshold per region, or a fixed number you choose. Then look at the binary result and the share of each class.
features.specific: Under 3 · Binarize, either tick Zonal thresholding (N/W/S/E) or set Manual threshold (0 = auto Otsu). The Binarize tab shows Method, Threshold(s) and Zonal in a banner, a Binarize Log, the Binarized Fisheye image (Canopy=0, Gap=1) with the threshold in its title, and Gap (sky) % and Canopy % metrics.
steps: Leave threshold at 0 for global Otsu, or tick Zonal for four sector thresholds
Or type a manual threshold value
Press Run Analysis
Open the Binarize tab and read the method, thresholds and Gap/Canopy %
Compare the downstream LAI in Canopy Attributes
serves_tasks: Compare automatic, per-region and fixed classification thresholds

features.name: Polar ring-and-sector sampling grid overlay
features.general: Divide a circular image into concentric angle bands and wedge sectors over a chosen angle range under a chosen projection model, and draw the grid on the image before values are averaged per cell.
features.specific: Under 4 · Gap Fraction, set Lens type (FC-E8 / equidistant), Max VZA, Start/End VZA, the Zenith rings slider (1–20) and the Azimuth segments slider (1–36). The Gap Fraction tab shows a banner (Lens | Rings | Segments | VZA range), a Gap Fraction Log and the 'Applied Rings & Segments' plot with yellow rings and sector lines over the binary image.
steps: Choose the lens projection model
Set start/end view zenith angle
Set the number of zenith rings and azimuth segments
Press Run Analysis
Check the ring/segment overlay in the Gap Fraction tab
serves_tasks: Restrict the range of view angles used
